name: sigma_hunt
description: Run a Sigma ruleset over event logs with one engine the host has (Zircolite or Hayabusa; either is enough) and return normalised detections: rule, level, time, event id, channel, record id and the matching record. A detection is a hypothesis; the record it points at is the evidence. Each invocation writes to a directory of its own under out_dir (hunt-<UTC time>-<id>; out_dir itself must be a place the run can write, work/<your id>/... in a VM or $OUT in a job, else it is refused naming the places), so an earlier run's result is never read as this one's and nothing is replaced. The engine's exit status is judged: a non-zero status, a stop by timeout_seconds, or a line of its result that cannot be read makes the run PARTIAL (status, complete, exit_code, malformed_lines with the lines kept whole in a file). The result is read as a stream, line by line when its first line begins an object (so a damaged first line costs one line) and value by value otherwise, and what stops making sense is copied to the unreadable-lines file in chunks, never held in memory; it is normalised into detections.jsonl, sorted by level and time with a bounded-memory merge. The level words each engine writes are ranked (Hayabusa's crit, med and info among them); a detection whose level is not known is kept, shown first and counted under unknown_levels, never dropped by min_level. The ruleset you name is recorded by digest and the engine's version is recorded where it prints one; without a ruleset the engine's bundled rules are used and not recorded. The engine's whole stdout, stderr and logs are kept in files it names. SENSITIVE: every detection carries the whole record it matched, which can hold command lines, script text or other secrets; run it as a job with secret_output: true when the logs may. The program runs in the tool's own process group (never a session of its own), so the harness ending the tool ends it; the tool's own deadline kills it and what it started, and SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP do the same and the answer is then status interrupted.

path.description: An .evtx file or a directory of them

engine.description: auto (default; Zircolite when both are present), zircolite or hayabusa

rules.description: A ruleset file or directory; the engine's bundled rules are used when omitted

min_level.description: informational, low, medium, high or critical (default medium); a detection with a level that is not one of these (or none) is kept and counted under unknown_levels

out_dir.description: A directory under your own work/<your id>/ (work/extracted/<id>/, work/quarantine/<id>/ and tool-output/<id>/ also work; in a job, under $OUT): any other place is refused with the places that work named. Each run writes into hunt-<UTC time>-<id> inside it: the engine's result, its whole stdout and stderr, its logs, every detection (detections.jsonl) and any unreadable line

limit.description: Detections to return inline (default 200, an inline page size); all of them, normalised, are in detections.jsonl in the run directory, named in all_detections

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this long (default 900, at most 1000)
